sentence_start: Quantities are in the non-dimensional units of the computations
problem: 31 words whose length is carried by the inline unit definitions; the sentence is otherwise a table note and cannot be shortened without losing the definitions.
suggested_fix: Quantities are in the non-dimensional units of the computations ($\rho=c_1=c_v=1$, lengths in $c_1/\omega_*$, times in $1/\omega_*$, so $k_{\rm cond}=1$) unless stated otherwise.

sentence_start: A new model or solver should join the registry with
problem: 42 words containing a three-item requirement list inside one sentence; the third item ("a statement of what a pass does \emph{not} establish") is the most unusual and is buried.

suggested_fix: Except for B01 and B08, whose references are symbolic, the reference solutions are closed forms or an independent algorithm rather than a second independently written codebase. An independent implementation by another group remains open.

sentence_start: Combined with energy balance it yields a parabolic equation
problem: 41 words with three clauses stacked on one colon-plus-appositive; the reader loses the subject ("it") before the point arrives.
suggested_fix: Combined with the energy balance, Fourier's law yields a parabolic equation, and that equation has a physically uncomfortable property: a temperature disturbance applied at one point changes the temperature everywhere else at the same instant, however small the change may be.

sentence_start: For slow processes in bulk matter, this instantaneous response differs immeasurably
problem: Vague comparative ("differs immeasurably") plus a counterfactual that never states the comparison; the sentence asserts rather than states the physics.
suggested_fix: For slow processes in bulk matter this instantaneous response cannot be distinguished from that of a slower, finite-speed carrier of heat.

sentence_start: They now form one of the largest strands
problem: Empty magnitude ("a very large body of theoretical work") added to an already evaluative clause; two vague quantifiers in one sentence.
suggested_fix: They now form one of the largest strands of continuum mechanics, with a correspondingly large theoretical literature.

sentence_start: It inherits the infinite thermal signal speed
problem: "It" follows a sentence about Danilovskaya and Chadwick--Sneddon, so the nearest noun is the wrong antecedent for the classical coupled theory.
suggested_fix: The classical coupled theory inherits the infinite thermal signal speed.

sentence_start: Two further developments widened the field
problem: One-line paragraph used as a hinge; it announces a list that then arrives two paragraphs later, with the piezoelectric sentence and the nanoscale sentence in between.
suggested_fix: Two further developments widened the field: coupling to further physical fields, and enrichment of the elastic law itself.

sentence_start: The literature that results is large
problem: Awkward nominalization ("the literature that results"); the verb "result" is being forced into an adjectival role.
suggested_fix: The resulting literature is large and still growing.

sentence_start: That is the period in which the number of named
problem: "That" points back to a date range two sentences earlier; the referent is a pair of counts, not a period.
suggested_fix: That period saw the number of named heat-conduction models for thermoelastic waves multiply.

sentence_start: in this review
problem: Self-reference is split across "this review" (41 occurrences, including 11 "of this review" and 11 "in this review"), "this paper" (7) and "this work" (2); the variation is not systematic, and the density draws attention to the author.

sentence_start: \textbf{Unreliable folklore about limits and stability
problem: The bold lead-in and its sentence carry 35 words; the sentence then lists three parallel questions after a colon and cannot be read at speed. (Word count includes the run-in heading, which is house style; the list itself is content and must stay.)
suggested_fix: Papers repeat several statements without re-deriving them. These are which parameter limits reduce one model to another, which parameter ranges are stable, and how the wave branches should be labeled.

sentence_start: This review covers the following ground
problem: Pure boilerplate transition; the following list has four items, which the sentence does not tell the reader.
suggested_fix: The review covers four strands of work.

problem: 36 words in one sentence with a four-item parenthetical wedged between subject and verb; the reader reaches the verb after the list.

These are the coupled dispersion polynomial, the Debye form of weak-coupling damping, the Green--Naghdi type-II wave speeds and the reductions of Table~\ref{tab:param}.

sentence_start: Each row names the place where the contribution is delivered, so that the claim can be checked rather than believed
problem: 31 words with two coordinate clauses, and a slightly adversarial aside ("rather than believed") that is aimed at other authors rather than at the reader.
suggested_fix: Each row names the place where the contribution is delivered. The evidence column names only what this paper actually contains, so that a claim can be checked rather than taken on trust.

sentence_start: C5 needs one caution

sentence_start: A statement derived here is presented as a derivation

problem: 41 words (including the run-in heading) in one sentence; the parenthetical list of fields interrupts the main clause.
suggested_fix: A DOI printed in the reference list has been checked against a bibliographic record for the same work (author, title, journal, volume, pages). The verification level recorded for that entry (R0--R3) says how far the check went.

problem: 34 words in a balanced pair of clauses; the second clause repeats the first with a negation, so the sentence is twice as long as its content.

sentence_start: The protocol has limits, and they are part of it
problem: Self-referential loop ("limits ... are part of it"); the sentence opens the closing paragraph of the protocol but says nothing the reader can act on.

sentence_start: around one heat-flux template with three lags
problem: The object is called the "heat-flux template" (8 times), "the template" (44 times) and "the family"; a member of it is called a "heat law" (43 times) and a "heat-flux law" (17 times), so template and member are sometimes hard to tell apart.

sentence_start: Green--Naghdi (Sec.~\ref{sec:part_theories})
problem: The classification figure abbreviates section references as "Sec.~" while the text writes "Section~" or uses `\cref`; inside one figure, three of the six node labels use the abbreviation.

sentence_start: In an isotropic solid, shear waves are unaltered by thermal effects
problem: 33 words in a three-part semicolon series whose last item changes subject; the reader has to re-parse to see that all three are properties of the classical theory.
suggested_fix: In an isotropic solid, shear waves are unaltered by thermal effects. Two distinct dilatational waves exist, both dispersed and attenuated \citep{Deresiewicz1957}, and the temperature field obeys a diffusive equation rather than a wave equation.

sentence_start: Gurtin and Pipkin \citep{GurtinPipkin1968} developed a general theory of heat conduction with finite wave speeds
problem: Figure and table references mix bare `\cref` (11 + 17) with `Fig.~\ref` (1) and `Table~\ref` (10); the hard-coded forms break when a label is renamed and look different in print.
suggested_fix: ... developed a general theory of heat conduction with finite wave speeds, starting from the same objection to the parabolic equation.

sentence_start: It was studied systematically as an evolution problem
problem: "It" refers to the Moore--Gibson--Thompson equation, but the preceding sentence is about the acoustics of relaxing gases, so the reader must guess.
suggested_fix: The Moore--Gibson--Thompson equation was studied systematically as an evolution problem \citep{MarchandMcDevittTriggiani2012,LasieckaWang2015MGT,DellOroLasieckaPata2016MGT,DellOroPata2016Viscoelasticity} and then brought into thermoelasticity by Quintanilla \citep{Quintanilla2019,Bazarra2021MGTradial}.

sentence_start: Micropolar and microcontinuum theories \citep{Eringen1966a,TauchertClausAriman1968,Eringen1999}, materials with voids \c
problem: 32 words with a four-element subject list held together by one verb; the sentence is a catalogue in the middle of a narrative paragraph.
suggested_fix: Micropolar and microcontinuum theories \citep{Eringen1966a,TauchertClausAriman1968,Eringen1999}, materials with voids \citep{Nunziato1979,Cowin1983,Iesan1986} and thermopiezoelectricity \citep{Mindlin1974Thermopiezo,Nowacki1978,Chandrasekharaiah1984} extended the mechanical content, usually with the heat law kept as an independent module. Thermoelastic diffusion and magneto-thermoelasticity did the same.

sentence_start: Three largely independent axes sort the recent literature
problem: 49 words in one sentence, with the three axes named twice (first as a summary, then as a list of parenthetical glosses).
suggested_fix: Three largely independent axes sort the recent literature on wave problems in thermoelastic and multiphysics media. These are the \emph{heat-flux law}, the \emph{constitutive enrichment} (nonlocal, gradient, microstructural, multiphysics), and the \emph{problem type} (plane waves, surface waves, reflection and transmission, transient response).

sentence_start: That modularity is what makes a unified treatment possible
problem: "That modularity" and "it" both look back over two sentences to a different claim, and the sentence is evaluative rather than informative.
suggested_fix: Because the two modules are independent, one treatment covers both, and every claim then needs a limit check.

sentence_start: \end{summarybox} The papers of Chiri\c{t}\u{a} and co-workers \citep{Chirita2016,Tibullo2017} examine thermodynamic comp
problem: 35 words in a compound sentence that joins a literature attribution to a result of this paper; two unrelated statements share one sentence and one citation group.
suggested_fix: The papers of Chiri\c{t}\u{a} and co-workers \citep{Chirita2016,Tibullo2017} examine thermodynamic compatibility and continuous dependence of the time-differential lag models. The stability computation reported in Section~\ref{sec:lags} shows how strongly the truncation order matters.

sentence_start: \label{sec:foundations} This section collects the balance laws
problem: 34-word section opening that lists four items and then claims the section is self-contained; the list delays the only sentence the reader needs (what the section is for).
suggested_fix: The section collects four things: the balance laws, the thermodynamic structure of linear thermoelasticity, the reasons Fourier's law fails for fast processes, and the heat-flux template that organizes the rest of the review.

sentence_start: The presentation is self-contained, so later sections can cite equation numbers
problem: "so that" occurs 27 times and "so the" 30 times; together they give almost every paragraph the same causal cadence.
suggested_fix: The presentation is self-contained; later sections cite equation numbers instead of rederiving them.

sentence_start: Here lies the difficulty with lagged and relaxed laws
problem: Inverted archaic opening ("Here lies ...") closing a subsection; the sentence ends the paragraph on a pointer to another section rather than on the point just derived.
suggested_fix: The difficulty with lagged and relaxed laws arises here (Section~\ref{sec:beyond}).

sentence_start: For processes on the time scale of the carrier relaxation it does
problem: Paragraph-final sentence whose "it" has no local antecedent and whose "does" stands for a whole predicate; the paragraph ends on a riddle.
suggested_fix: Fourier's law fails for processes on the time scale of the carrier relaxation.

sentence_start: Green and Lindsay \citep{Green1972} keep a single temperature but let the free energy and the stress depend on $\dot\the
problem: 35 words; the "so that" clause restates what the main clause has already said, so the sentence is longer than its content.
suggested_fix: Green and Lindsay \citep{Green1972} keep a single temperature but let the free energy and the stress depend on $\dot\theta$. The entropy and stress relations then carry temperature-rate terms.

sentence_start: The relaxation times $\tau_0,\tau_1$ used in this review are the notation of the later literature for those rate coeffic
problem: 35 words with three coordinate statements about notation, flux form and isotropy; notational housekeeping occupies a full sentence and the reader cannot tell which part matters.
suggested_fix: The relaxation times $\tau_0,\tau_1$ used in this review follow the notation of the later literature for those rate coefficients. The heat flux is taken in its Fourier form, as is usual for the isotropic case.

sentence_start: Green--Lindsay theory (Section~\ref{sec:gl}) changes the energy and constitutive equations and so is not a row; for frac
problem: 34 words in a semicolon compound that mixes a table exception with a generalization; the two halves answer different questions.
suggested_fix: Green--Lindsay theory (Section~\ref{sec:gl}) changes the energy and constitutive equations, so it is not a row of the table. For fractional and memory-dependent models, $G(s)$ keeps the same structure with $s$ replaced by non-integer powers or by kernel transforms (Section~\ref{sec:memory}).

sentence_start: They differ from the flux $q_i-\sigma_{ij}\dot u_j$
problem: "They" can refer to the availability flux, to its flux $P_i$, or to the fluxes of the previous sentence; two competing plural antecedents sit in the same paragraph.
suggested_fix: The availability flux differs from the flux $q_i-\sigma_{ij}\dot u_j$ of the \emph{total} internal energy, whose heat-flux part is first order in the disturbance and averages to zero over a period.

sentence_start: They coincide with the referential quantities of the linearized theory
problem: Third consecutive sentence opening with a bare pronoun in the same paragraph; the reader has to track three plural antecedents across four sentences.
suggested_fix: The two flux definitions coincide with the referential quantities of the linearized theory used elsewhere in this review only to first order in the disturbance, and the advection term below is of higher order.

sentence_start: The lag models of \cref{sec:lags} are usually justified by their formal structure
problem: Dismissive generalization ("usually justified by their formal structure") at the head of a section; it is an evaluation of other authors' motives without a citation.
suggested_fix: The lag models of \cref{sec:lags} are often introduced through their formal structure rather than from a kinetic argument.

sentence_start: This is the Cattaneo law with $\tau_q=\tau_R$, valid when the closure holds, that is, when the phonon mean free path
problem: One sentence carries the identification with Cattaneo, the closure condition, two small parameters and a validity range; four clauses chained by "when/so that".
suggested_fix: This is the Cattaneo law with $\tau_q=\tau_R$, valid when the closure holds. The closure requires the phonon mean free path to be small compared with the wavelength, so that $\omega\tau_R\ll1$ and $\ell_{\rm mfp}k\ll1$.

sentence_start: They explain these experiments within extended thermodynamics of phonons
problem: "They" and "these experiments" both point backwards without a named referent in the sentence; the paragraph has just introduced two competing phonon pictures.
suggested_fix: Guyer and Krumhansl explain these experiments within an extended thermodynamics of phonons.

sentence_start: It therefore lies outside the template of \cref{sec:foundations}
problem: Bare "It" opening a paragraph, referring to the Guyer--Krumhansl law introduced two paragraphs earlier; "therefore" then asks the reader to reconstruct the argument.
suggested_fix: The Guyer--Krumhansl law therefore lies outside the template of \cref{sec:foundations} and is treated separately in \cref{sec:size}.

sentence_start: Its role is to represent non-local (Knudsen-type) corrections
problem: The paper writes "nonlocal" 129 times and "non-local" 3 times in its own prose (the fourth occurrence is inside a verbatim catalogue title); both spellings are visible to a reader.
suggested_fix: Its role is to represent nonlocal (Knudsen-type) corrections at intermediate frequencies.

sentence_start: They are collected here with the conventions of this review
problem: Opening sentence of the section is a bare pronoun; what "they" are (the definitions) is only recoverable from the heading.
suggested_fix: The definitions are collected here with the conventions of this review, so that every statement about branches, damping and dispersion rests on a single definition.

sentence_start: That is the origin of the criterion used in \cref{sec:hyperbolic}
problem: "That" refers to an equation derived in the previous sentence and then to a criterion introduced later; the sentence compresses three steps into one pointer.
suggested_fix: This argument gives the criterion used in \cref{sec:hyperbolic}: finite signal speed requires $sG(s)$ to tend to a finite, non-zero limit.

sentence_start: \emph{Thermodynamic admissibility} asks whether the law is compatible with the second law
problem: The defining sentence of the section runs through the second law, internal state variables, the Clausius--Duhem inequality and two necessary conditions in one string of clauses; a definition should be short enough to be quoted.
suggested_fix: \emph{Thermodynamic admissibility} asks whether the law is compatible with the second law. For materials with internal state variables, the Clausius--Duhem inequality supplies the test, and two necessary conditions follow for any law of the template.

sentence_start: Solutions of the initial--boundary value problem are unique
problem: 31 words with a three-item parenthetical inserted between the claim and its consequence; the reader reaches "depend continuously" through a list of boundary conditions.
suggested_fix: Solutions of the initial--boundary value problem are unique under standard boundary conditions, that is, Dirichlet, Neumann or Robin conditions on each of the mechanical and thermal parts. They depend continuously on the data.

sentence_start: They are called types rather than ``waves''
problem: Sentence opens with "They" and then argues about terminology; the antecedent (the branches) is two sentences away, and the aside about naming reads as an apology.
suggested_fix: The branches are called types rather than ``waves'', because the classical thermal branch is a diffusive wave with $\Real k=\Imag k$, which attenuates by a factor $e^{-2\pi}$ per wavelength.

sentence_start: \label{eq:disp} \end{equation} Equation~\eqref{eq:disp} holds for every member of the template
problem: Equations are cited as `\eqref` (151 times), `\cref{eq:...}` (27), `Equation~\eqref` (3) and `Eq.~\eqref` (1); the last three make the surrounding style look inconsistent.
suggested_fix: \eqref{eq:disp} holds for every member of the template of Section~\ref{sec:framework-link}; Appendix~\ref{app:disp} gives a derivation and the symbolic check.

sentence_start: The classical theory is \emph{adiabatic} at low frequency and \emph{isothermal} at high frequency, because conduction ov
problem: 33 words in which the same idea is stated twice (efficient when short, negligible when long) with a condition in parentheses; circular phrasing ("conduction over a wavelength ... when the wavelength").
suggested_fix: The classical theory is \emph{adiabatic} at low frequency and \emph{isothermal} at high frequency, because conduction over a wavelength is efficient when the wavelength is short ($\alpha k^2\gg\omega$) and negligible when it is long.

sentence_start: For the metals of Table~\ref{tab:materials}, $\omega_*\sim10^{11}$--$10^{12}$\,rad/s, a lag time of order a picosecond t
problem: 32 words carrying a table reference, two numbers, an inference and an evaluative close ("the heat law then matters"); "therefore" glosses over the arithmetic the reader must do.
suggested_fix: For the metals of Table~\ref{tab:materials}, $\omega_*\sim10^{11}$--$10^{12}$\,rad/s. A lag time of order a picosecond then puts the product near order one at the \emph{bulk} damping peak, and the heat law matters there.

sentence_start: In a thin beam of thickness $h$ vibrating in flexure
problem: 44 words (including the run-in heading) with the geometry, the Zener relaxation time, the Debye form, the strength and Young's modulus in one sentence; the reader gets no sentence boundary before the citation.
suggested_fix: In a thin beam of thickness $h$ vibrating in flexure the temperature varies across the thickness with a thermal relaxation time $\tau_Z\simeq h^2/(\pi^2\alpha)$ (Zener). The damping then has the same Debye form with $\omega_*$ replaced by $1/\tau_Z$ and the relaxation strength $\Delta=E\alpha_T^2T_0/(\rho c)$, with Young's modulus $E$ \citep{Zener1937}.

sentence_start: The coupled problem no longer separates into shear and dilatational parts
problem: 32 words that state a loss (no separation), a gain (three branches) and a conditional (symmetric directions) in one breath; the conditional is the actionable part.
suggested_fix: The coupled problem no longer separates into shear and dilatational parts, but quasi-longitudinal, quasi-shear and thermal branches exist. Along symmetric directions the one-dimensional analysis above applies with the appropriate effective moduli.

sentence_start: Three predictions of the classical theory conflict with finite-speed heat transport
problem: 39 words, three items in a colon list, each with a parenthetical figure reference; the sentence is a table of contents rather than an argument.
suggested_fix: Three predictions of the classical theory conflict with finite-speed heat transport: the instantaneous thermal signal, the unbounded thermal phase speed (\Cref{fig:disp}c, black curve), and the monotonic growth of thermal attenuation with frequency.

sentence_start: It underestimates the loss for $x\gtrsim10$
problem: Bare "It" opening a paragraph, referring to the Zener form from the previous paragraph; the two candidate approximations in between are both "the form".
suggested_fix: The Zener form underestimates the loss for $x\gtrsim10$, where both decay as $x^{-1}$ but the exact solution has the larger coefficient, $12/\pi^2\approx1.22$ times that of the Zener form.

sentence_start: Let $\tau_0$ denote the flux relaxation time
problem: 32 words that define one symbol, give its two names and then define a second symbol with its own description; notation is delivered in running prose instead of a list.
suggested_fix: Let $\tau_0$ denote the flux relaxation time (Lord--Shulman) or the thermal relaxation time (Green--Lindsay, in the notation of the later literature). Let $\tau^\dagger$ be the lag that multiplies the thermal-stress and dilatation coupling.

sentence_start: The unified form of Dhaliwal and Sherief
problem: 32 words whose payload is a single contrast (which coupling term carries the time derivative), buried after a citation and a phrase about the level of the field equations.
suggested_fix: The unified form of Dhaliwal and Sherief \citep{Dhaliwal1980} makes the same point at the level of the field equations. The theories differ in which of the two coupling terms carries a time-derivative correction.

sentence_start: For solids the strongest evidence of wave-like heat propagation remains second sound at cryogenic temperatures \citep{Ac
problem: 30 words with two citation groups and a "rather than" contrast; the citation load sits between the claim and the contrast.
suggested_fix: For solids the strongest evidence of wave-like heat propagation remains second sound at cryogenic temperatures \citep{Ackerman1966,Jackson1970}. There the governing regime is the Guyer--Krumhansl hydrodynamic one \citep{GuyerKrumhansl1966II} rather than the simple Cattaneo law.

sentence_start: In the notation of Green and Lindsay \citep{Green1972}
problem: 42 words in one sentence that maps two notations, two equations and a restriction; the reader cannot hold the symbol correspondence across three "and" clauses.
suggested_fix: In the notation of Green and Lindsay \citep{Green1972}, $\tau_1$ is the coefficient $\alpha$ of $\dot\theta$ in the stress relation, and $\tau_0=h/d$ is the ratio of the coefficients of $\ddot\theta$ and $\dot\theta$ in the energy equation. Their restrictions $d\alpha-h\ge0$, $h>0$ (Eqs.~(4.14) and~(4.16) of that paper) give the ordering stated.

sentence_start: At the wave fronts the coupling is stronger than in LS
problem: 39 words in which the reason is given as a three-part balance of which symbol sits where; the causal chain is longer than the claim.
suggested_fix: At the wave fronts the coupling is stronger than in LS by the factor $\tau_1/\tau_0\ge1$. The temperature-rate term in the stress carries $\tau_1$, the thermal inertia carries $\tau_0$, and the strain-rate coupling in the energy equation carries no relaxation time.

sentence_start: Here the relation is \emph{exact at every frequency}
problem: Negative parallelism used as emphasis ("not merely asymptotically") plus a "Here" opener; the device recurs in the paper and adds no content.
suggested_fix: The relation is \emph{exact at every frequency}: the roots of the quadratic \eqref{eq:disp} with $G=k^*/s$ are non-dispersive.

sentence_start: At \emph{low} frequency $G\simeq k^*/s$ and the thermal branch has the type-II speed $c_*$; at \emph{high} frequency $G\
problem: 35 words in a two-part frequency contrast with a figure reference inside the second part; the figure callout breaks the parallel.
suggested_fix: At \emph{low} frequency $G\simeq k^*/s$ and the thermal branch has the type-II speed $c_*$. At \emph{high} frequency $G\to k$ and the branch becomes diffusive, so its phase speed is unbounded (\Cref{fig:family}, magenta curve), exactly as in the classical theory.

sentence_start: Chandrasekharaiah proved uniqueness for type II
problem: 32 words that list three separate results with four citation groups; the sentence is a bibliography paragraph in disguise and mixes a verb ("proved") with two passive clauses.
suggested_fix: Chandrasekharaiah proved uniqueness for type II \citep{Chandrasekharaiah1996}, and complete solutions for type II were given in \citep{Chandrasekharaiah1997}. The theory without energy dissipation for anisotropic and micropolar media was developed in \citep{Iesan1998,Quintanilla1999,Ciarletta1999,Quintanilla2002}.

sentence_start: For the type III system, Zhang and Zuazua \citep{ZhangZuazua2003} report that for most domains
problem: 45 words with three parallel "that" clauses whose qualifiers ("for most domains", "under suitable conditions", "for most domains in two space dimensions") differ in ways that are easy to miss.
suggested_fix: For the type III system, Zhang and Zuazua \citep{ZhangZuazua2003} report three results. For most domains the energy does not decay uniformly, under suitable conditions on the domain it decays exponentially, and in two space dimensions the energy of smooth solutions decays polynomially.

sentence_start: An attribution is a claim about a source

sentence_start: For the damping and the speed of the elastic-type branch, the question is answered by computing the relative difference
problem: 36 words where the question, the two models compared and the two dimensionless numbers are all in one sentence, with the figure callout at the end.
suggested_fix: For the damping and the speed of the elastic-type branch, the question is answered by comparing the Lord--Shulman and classical predictions over the plane of two dimensionless numbers, the frequency $\omega/\omega_*$ and the lag $\tau_0\omega_*$ (\Cref{fig:regime}).

sentence_start: A paper that reports a ``strong effect of the relaxation time on the phase speed'' for realistic lags and ultrasonic fre
problem: 45 words with a colon followed by a capital "A", so two sentences are welded together; the first half also contains a quoted claim and a whole clause of qualification.
suggested_fix: A paper that reports a ``strong effect of the relaxation time on the phase speed'' for realistic lags and ultrasonic frequencies should therefore be examined for its choice of nondimensionalization. A nondimensional lag chosen for plotting convenience can be far larger than any physical value.

sentence_start: of DPL, not to the first-order template; no unstable root
problem: 37 words that state a correction, an attribution of the condition to a variant, a negative result and its epistemic status in one sentence.
suggested_fix: The $\tau_T\ge\tau_q/2$ condition belongs to the second-order-in-$\tau_q$ truncation of DPL, not to the first-order template. No unstable root of the first-order version was found in the numerical sweep of Section~\ref{sec:lags}, which is evidence and not a proof.

sentence_start: The frequency thresholds quoted in this review answer different questions
problem: 66 words in a single sentence listing three thresholds, each with its own condition and section reference; this is the most information-dense sentence in the synthesis.
suggested_fix: The frequency thresholds quoted in this review answer different questions and are not one universal boundary. The range $\omega\tau_q\lesssim0.3$ is where the Taylor truncations reproduce the thermal-branch wavenumber of the exact delay law (Section~\ref{sec:delayfid}); $\omega\tau<0.1$ together with $\omega/\omega_*<0.1$ is the rule used to call Fourier adequate in the scenario table.

sentence_start: It is a guide, not a substitute for checking against data
problem: Aphoristic closing sentence of the decision-guide subsection, again in the "it is X, not Y" frame used throughout the paper.
suggested_fix: The guide is a starting point, and it does not replace a check against measured data.

sentence_start: \label{sec:atlas} Wave problems treated in the literature are collected here
problem: 37 words (heading included) with two purposes chained by "so that" and two objects ("geometry, heat law and coupling" and "what the source actually shows").
suggested_fix: Wave problems treated in the literature are collected here. For each one the table gives the geometry, heat law and coupling that have been studied, and what the source actually shows.

sentence_start: It is limited to papers available to the author in full text
problem: Bare "It" opening a paragraph, referring to the atlas table by implication; "papers available to the author" is an authorial aside.
suggested_fix: The atlas is limited to papers available to the author in full text, and it is not an exhaustive survey.

sentence_start: They are kept because they are the model problems used in this review
problem: Bare "They" with two possible antecedents (the redundant entries, the model problems); the sentence also repeats "they are" twice.
suggested_fix: The redundant entries are kept because they are the model problems used in this review, but they are not counted as independent evidence.

sentence_start: They are kept because they are the model problems used in this review
problem: "this review" appears 41 times (plus "this paper" 7 and "this work" 2), often twice in a paragraph; the self-reference is the single most repeated phrase in the manuscript.
suggested_fix: They are kept because they are the model problems used here, but they are not counted as independent evidence.

sentence_start: That single axis collapses independent commitments into one word
problem: Bare "That single axis" and an evaluative verb ("collapses") standing in for the argument; the axis is named in the previous sentence, which discusses two.
suggested_fix: The single label collapses three independent commitments into one word.

sentence_start: \Cref{sec:synthesis} compares families; this section says what a family \emph{is} as a coordinate, so that a new model c
problem: 324 of 1592 prose sentences (about 20 per cent) begin with "The"; combined with the uniform paragraph shape (claim, reason, consequence), it gives a monotone rhythm.
suggested_fix: \Cref{sec:synthesis} compares families; this section defines what a family \emph{is} as a coordinate, so that a new model can be placed in the taxonomy.

sentence_start: Such models therefore cannot be ranked against the template's members
problem: "Such models" has no antecedent in the paragraph, and "therefore" points to an argument made in a figure caption.
suggested_fix: Models that fall on a different point of Axis~2 therefore cannot be ranked against the template's members by setting a lag to zero.

sentence_start: In the five-axis scheme below they correspond mainly to the mathematical axis
problem: 30 words opening a paragraph with a bare "they" and a forward reference ("below"); "correspond mainly to" leaves the reader to decide how much is not covered.
suggested_fix: In the five-axis scheme below, these commitments correspond mainly to the mathematical axis (Axis~2), both for the heat law and for the local, nonlocal or gradient form of the elastic law.

sentence_start: It fixes which conserved quantities and driving fields exist before any approximation
problem: Bare "It" for the physical axis, whose name appeared two paragraphs earlier; the sentence is the justification for the axis and is easy to misread.
suggested_fix: The physical axis fixes which conserved quantities and driving fields exist, before any approximation is made.

sentence_start: A difference in the mathematical axis changes the governing operator
problem: 30 words in a balanced contrast whose two halves are not parallel (one changes an operator, the other an epistemic status); the abstraction is high.
suggested_fix: A difference in the mathematical axis changes the governing operator and invalidates most direct comparisons. A difference in the validation axis changes only the epistemic status of the conclusion.

sentence_start: A taxonomy earns its place only if it changes a decision
problem: Self-justifying frame ("earns its place", "changes three") introduces the subsection; it argues with an imagined critic rather than with the reader.
suggested_fix: The taxonomy changes three decisions in this review.

sentence_start: It fixes the order in which \cref{sec:synthesis} compares families
problem: A 30-plus-word sentence whose subject is "It", whose object is the order of another section, and which then states why yet another section insists on a definition; three cross-references in one sentence.
suggested_fix: The taxonomy fixes the order in which \cref{sec:synthesis} compares families. It is also why \cref{sec:interfaces} insists that an energy flux be defined consistently with the model before ratios are compared (see \cref{sec:eqregister}).

sentence_start: For the first-order template no unstable root has been found numerically
problem: 51 words (heading included) with the numerical result, its scope, the missing analytical statement and the front-speed condition in one sentence.
suggested_fix: For the first-order template no unstable root has been found numerically for DPL in a finite sweep of positive lags, and an analytical statement is lacking. The condition under which the thermal front has finite speed, the behavior of $sG(s)$ at large $s$, has been identified.

sentence_start: What applied authors still lack is a complete analytical statement
problem: 46 words whose subject is a pseudo-cleft ("What applied authors still lack is ...") and whose predicate then lists parameters and a coupling in a parenthetical.
suggested_fix: Applied authors still lack a complete analytical statement of well-posedness, decay and front structure for the coupled TPL and MGT systems with all parameters positive. What is needed is the conditions on $(\tau_q,\tau_T,\tau_v,k,k^*)$ together with the role of the coupling $\varepsilon$, in a form they can use directly.

sentence_start: Authors compute combinations of nonlocal or gradient elasticity
problem: 36 words (heading included) that contrast how often a combination is computed with how rarely it is validated; "far more often than" is doing the argumentative work.
suggested_fix: Combinations of nonlocal or gradient elasticity with hyperbolic or memory heat laws are computed far more often than they are validated against lattice dynamics or atomistic simulation.

sentence_start: A set of agreed benchmark problems, namely the heat pulse
problem: 39 words (heading included) in which the benchmark problems are listed by appositive and the benefit is stated in a modal clause.
suggested_fix: A set of agreed benchmark problems, namely the heat pulse, thermal shock, Rayleigh wave and interface problems of this review, with reference solutions at specified precision, would improve the reliability of numerical codes.

sentence_start: That organization buys three kinds of result
problem: Informal commercial metaphor ("buys") in the first sentence of the Conclusions, where the register should be formal.
suggested_fix: That organization yields three kinds of result.

sentence_start: It gives a dispersion polynomial for linear homogeneous media
problem: 39 words with a chain of three relative clauses ("from which ... and which shows ... and only for ..."); the final condition is attached to the wrong noun for most readers.
suggested_fix: It gives a dispersion polynomial for linear homogeneous media and rational heat laws, from which comparative speeds, attenuation and thermoelastic damping follow. The polynomial shows that the heat law affects damping long before it affects speed, and only for $\omega\tau\gtrsim0.05$.

sentence_start: It gives problem-level results: finite fronts and surface jumps
problem: 44 words with a five-item colon list of results; the list items are of different kinds (phenomena, structures, dependencies, distinctions).
suggested_fix: It gives problem-level results: finite fronts and surface jumps in heat pulses, the structure of thermoelastic Rayleigh waves, the renormalization by piezoelectric coupling, the calibration dependence of nonlocal lengths, and the distinction between net energy flux and mode-by-mode fractions at interfaces in lossy media.

sentence_start: The unified notation, the verified reductions, the pitfalls checklist
problem: 37 words in the closing sentence, which lists four deliverables and two purposes in parallel; the final clause ("so that effort goes where it is most needed") is a vague close.
suggested_fix: The unified notation, the verified reductions, the pitfalls checklist and the decision guide are there so that readers can choose, justify and check models. The open problems are there so that effort goes where it is most needed.

sentence_start: \label{sec:conclusions} Generalized thermoelasticity is a family organized by the function $G(s)$
problem: 34 words (heading included) that define the family, add choices of elastic law and fields, and negate an alternative in one sentence.
suggested_fix: Generalized thermoelasticity is a family organized by the function $G(s)$ that relates heat flux to temperature gradient, together with choices of elastic law and added fields. It is not a collection of unrelated theories.

sentence_start: The comparisons in this review were limited more often by what the original papers report
problem: Passive complaint about the literature ("were limited ... by what the original papers report") opens a section of recommendations; it tells the reader about other authors before it tells them what to do.
suggested_fix: What the original papers report limited the comparisons in this review more often than the models themselves did.

sentence_start: Give the model in the template of \cref{sec:foundations}
problem: 38 words (heading included) with a conditional alternative, three follow-on objects and a purpose clause; a recommendation should be one instruction per sentence.
suggested_fix: Give the model in the template of \cref{sec:foundations}, or state where it departs from it. Then $G(s)$, the polynomial of \cref{eq:unified} and the limit $\omega\to\infty$ follow without a reading of the derivation.

sentence_start: \textbf{The material source and the status of the parameters.} Say whether a lag time or fractional order is measured
problem: 39 words (heading included) giving a three-way classification and then a rule about tables; the two halves are separate instructions.
suggested_fix: Say whether a lag time or fractional order is measured, estimated by a stated argument, or assigned for illustration. Illustrative values should not share a table with measured ones.

sentence_start: They illustrate mechanisms and should be repeated
problem: Bare "They" in the closing sentence of the limitations subsection, referring to the computations, and "before design use" is a compressed instruction.
suggested_fix: The computations illustrate mechanisms and should be repeated with measured parameters before design use.

sentence_start: Generative AI tools were used in preparing this manuscript
problem: 45 words in a single sentence that lists four uses of the tools; the list is a run of parallel "for ..." phrases with no boundaries.
suggested_fix: Generative AI tools were used in preparing this manuscript: for drafting and language editing, for writing and running the verification computations, for checking notation and cross-references, and for literature and claim checks whose results are summarized in the evidence protocol (\cref{sec:evidence_protocol}).

sentence_start: Not every cited work was read page by page, and the claim register
problem: The checking apparatus is named "the register" (23 times), "the evidence protocol", "the claim register" (once here) and "the equation register"; a reader cannot tell whether these are one device or four.
suggested_fix: Not every cited work was read page by page, and the register records which attributions were checked against the printed source.
